title: Break the Conditioning with: Nietzschean REDPILLS
summary: Educated Barbarian episode interpreting aphorisms from chapter 4 of Beyond Good and Evil as 'red pills', moving from principles to judgment, morality and nihilism. NH argues principles and morals must be questioned and owned, hatred is the weapon of the weak, and comfort without struggle breeds nihilism and depression.
claims: Most internet red pills are bogus contrarian one-liners that leave followers depressed and smug while knowing a tiny fraction of the truth
Reducing philosophy and self-improvement to Instagram quotes like 'never give up' vulgarizes them; the concept behind the line must be explained
Principles are subjective expressions of individual sensibility; two men with the same principles pursue different ends
An idea swallowed without understanding is only half effective and poisons the one who takes it

Principles you never questioned were probably installed by someone else; question them constantly but do not drop them just because they become uncomfortable, since their job is to protect you from short-term pleasures
Forcing everyone into the same principles to obtain equal outcomes is a corruption of democracy that destroys individuality
Judge people by the long-term consequences of their actions, not by the intentions they display; whoever wears a mask too long becomes the mask
Disinterested deeds do not exist: appearing selfless is itself a benefit, and every act is an expression of will to power
Constantly trying to grow your body, soul, influence and wealth is a sign of health; ideologies that discourage it are toxic and most people make themselves too small
Love and sympathy are necessarily discriminating; sympathy for all is a lie, and people preaching universal love are often the cruelest toward those they disapprove of
Hatred is only felt toward equals or superiors; the superior feels disgust or domination, so accusations of hate mostly come from the weak as a moral weapon and shield
Killing without hate, as in bureaucratic genocides decided on statistics, produces far more victims than hate-driven violence
Nietzsche did not reject usefulness, only the claim that one's method is automatically 'for the greater good'
All training is functional for something, just as every philosophy is good for some goal; the real question is which goal
Knowledge or morality pursued for its own sake is a trap; a philosophy that is not useful to you should be let go
Your moral values were installed by your era; people who condemn ancestors would have shared their views had they been born then
Elites push moral codes that benefit them and rarely follow those codes themselves
Unlike Nietzsche, NH believes everyone, not just rare individuals, can break their conditioning and define their own values, which is why he makes philosophy videos
When a moral drive has nothing left to act on, it turns on its host, like a pack of wild dogs in his mountain village that turned on each other once prey ran out
Unquestioned morals become cancerous and make Western society destroy itself from within
Comfort without challenge makes life harder; exertion and pain are necessary for fulfilment, and much depression is nihilism that pills mask without fixing the root
Pleasure is biological bait: the real benefit of lifting is the effort before the endorphin high, not the high itself; chasing pleasure for its own sake leads to degeneracy
Happiness is a byproduct of struggle; pursuing it directly breeds apathy and kills the will to pursue anything
Nietzsche was an anti-nihilist; calling yourself a nihilist means you gave up, and cynicism is not being red-pilled
Welfare-state comfort with no danger and nothing to strive for produces people who cannot define their own values
Insanity is rare in individuals but the rule in groups; groupthink takes away free will and common sense
